messages:
ashley: Quick q re: calibration set for quant evals — what's everyone using for fp8/int8/GPTQ/AWQ bakeoffs?

mike: For GPTQ/AWQ runs I usually sample ~50k tokens from prod prompts + 2k doc-level examples. Works decent but not systematic.

priya: Would prefer stratified by token length & task (chat, instruct, code). Short prompt heavy sets bias metrics.

ashley: Agree. Thinking tiers: short Q&A (<50 tokens), multi-turn chat (50-500), long context (>500). Keep code examples separate.

sam: How many prompts per tier? budget is limited for full-precision baselines.

ashley: Target ~1k prompts per tier => ~6k total. We can augment with paraphrases for variance in open-gen tasks.

priya: Paraphrase augmentation helps but watch label drift for closed-answer evals (arithmetic, exact-match). Freeze those.

mike: For closed-answer tasks we freeze eval prompts and only use paraphrases for open-gen diversity (summaries, style).

ashley: eval-bot, can you queue a quick accuracy delta run: int8-gptq vs fp16 on the current candidate calibration set?

eval-bot: Run queued: compare int8-gptq vs fp16 on 'calib_v2' (6k prompts). ETA ~22m. job_id: jb-4521

ashley: Also adding a small API-style framing subset (system+user+assistant) to catch role-conditioning issues.

priya: Suggestion: include targeted prompts known to regress under AWQ (lists, tables, code blocks, long numbered steps).

mike: We should track: exact-match, F1, BLEU, and avg_logprob_shift per token. Logprob drift often predicts hallucination rate.

ashley: Yep — add metrics 'avg_logprob_delta' and 'response_len_delta' to the dashboard. Alert on >2% EM drop per tier.

eval-bot: Job jb-4521 complete. Summary: int8-gptq median EM delta -1.8% (worse), AWQ -2.6%, FP8 prototype -0.9%. Details: https://redwood.internal/evals/jb-4521

priya: FP8 looking interesting. Can you provide per-tier breakdown?

eval-bot: Per-tier deltas: short: -0.5%, mult-turn: -2.3%, long: -3.4%, code: -4.1% (highest regression).

sam: Code regressions make sense. We should expand code-focused calibration and include LM objective data during quantization (nll on code tokens).

mike: For GPTQ we can try a code-specific calibrator + bias-correction. AWQ also exposes per-layer tuning — try that on layer types with high sensitivity.

ashley: Action items: (1) bump code prompts to 2k, (2) add 1k instruction-paraphrases for open-gen, (3) rerun FP8/INT8/AWQ/GPTQ with updated cal set. I'll loop in infra for more GPU.

priya: I'll draft a short prompt curation playbook (tiers, sampling rules, banned prompts, augmentation rules) and share in #eng-ml.

ashley: Perfect. @mike can you coordinate with eng-infra for provisioning? :thumbsup:

mike: On it — requesting extra GPU hours and queue priority, cc @eng-infra.

ashley: Closing loop — if you have any 'nightmare' prompts that always regress, drop them here so we can add targeted tests.
